record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: For an infinite bipartite r-regular graph G, let h_G(p) be its p-matching entropy. Is h_G(p) always at least f(p,r) = 1/2 times (p log r - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (r-p) log(1-p/r)) for every p in [0,1]? The source explicitly reports this asymptotic lower matching conjecture as proved in the cited literature.

evidence.quote: The asymptotic lower matching conjecture, abbreviated ALMC, claims that for any r-regular bipartite infinite graph G the following inequality holds [23]: hG(p) ≥ f(p, r) for all p ∈ [0, 1].
The proof of the ALMC is given in [27].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite $r$-regular bipartite graph. For each $n$, let $G_n$ be a finite $r$-regular bipartite subgraph of $G$ obtained by an exhausting sequence, and let $m_k(G_n)$ denote the number of matchings of $G_n$ that cover exactly $k$ vertices on each side. For $p \in [0,1]$, define the $p$-matching entropy of $G$ by
$$h_G(p) \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{|V(G_n)|}\log m_{\lfloor p\,|V(G_n)|/2 \rfloor}(G_n),$$
assuming the limit exists (for instance when $G$ has a vertex-transitive automorphism group or admits a Benjamini–Schramm-type limiting structure). Define
$$f(p,r) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\Big( p\log r - p\log p - 2(1-p)\log(1-p) + (r-p)\log\!\big(1-\tfrac{p}{r}\big) \Big).$$
Prove or disprove: for every infinite $r$-regular bipartite graph $G$ and every $p\in[0,1]$,
$$h_G(p) \;\geq\; f(p,r).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Asymptotic Lower Matching Conjecture (ALMC), originally formulated by Friedland, Krop, and Markström, was proved by Péter Csikvári (and related work by Gurvits) using the theory of stable polynomials and matching measures. It is therefore considered solved.

status_evidence.snippet: We prove the Friedland–Krop–Markström Asymptotic Lower Matching Conjecture for r-regular bipartite graphs.
